title: Humane technology as a recurring theme
body: Across VantaAI, NeuroBridge, fAImer, and LawGorithm, Anita's work consistently chooses calmer, safer, and more accessible defaults. Detection systems aim to reduce harm; adaptive interfaces aim to reduce cognitive load; tools for low-connectivity contexts aim to reduce exclusion.

title: Graph theory and optimization across the stack
body: Anita has solved 400+ DSA problems (230+ LeetCode, 170+ Codeforces), with a particular focus on graph theory and optimization. This shows up in applied work — most directly in DelAI's graph-based routing, and as backend modeling intuition across other projects.

title: Accessibility and adaptive interfaces
body: NeuroBridge is the most explicit example: a modular adaptive-support platform for neurodivergent users, with ASD and ADHD support surfaces built around emotional safety and accessibility-first UX. The same accessibility instinct appears in the multilingual / offline-first design of fAImer.

title: Backend systems, REST APIs, and modular architecture
body: Multiple projects (VantaAI, LawGorithm, fAImer, NeuroBridge) rely on REST API surfaces and modular backend services — built primarily with Python (FastAPI), Node.js (Express), and standard relational + Firebase/Supabase storage.
